html:
The Dinka are the largest ethnic group of South Sudan, a Nilotic people of the plains around the Sudd swamps of the White Nile, whose way of life centres on cattle.

They move their herds between dry-season camps by the rivers and wet-season villages on higher ground. Cattle pay bride wealth, settle disputes, and are named and praised in songs, and young men take names from their favourite oxen. Their prophets and spear masters held religious authority.

The Dinka suffered heavily in the civil war, and many leaders of the southern movement, among them John Garang and Salva Kiir, are Dinka. Rivalry with the Nuer shaped the civil war of 2013.
sum: The Dinka are the largest ethnic group of South Sudan, a Nilotic people of the plains around the Sudd swamps of the White Nile, whose way of life centres on cattle.
